la:noun:onus.html:
ŏnus (in good MSS. also wr. hŏnus), ĕris, n.
etym. dub.; cf. Sanscr. anas, a wagon for freight
,
a load, burden (cf. pondus).
Lit.
In gen.: oneris maximi pondus,: onus sustinere,: cum gravius dorso subiit onus (asellus), Hor S. 1, 9, 20: tanti oneris turris,: ad minimum redigi onus, Ov M. 14, 149.—
In partic.
Of goods, baggage, etc., a load, lading, freight, cargo: insula Delos, quo omnes undique cum mercibus atque oneribus commeabant,: onera afferuntur,: (naves) ad onera et ad multitudinem jumentorum transportandam paulo latiores,: jumentis onera deponere,loads, packs,.—
Poet., the burden of the womb, the fœtus, embryo: gravidi ventris,; ; ; . —
The excrements: ciborum onera reddere,: duri ventris solvere,.—
Trop
A burden, in respect of property, i. e. a tax or an expense (usually in the plur.): municipium maximis oneribus pressum,: haec onera in dites a pauperibus inclinata,: patria,: haerere in explicandis oneribus,: oneribus novis turbantur provinciae,.—
A load, burden, weight, charge, trouble, difficulty of any kind (so most freq. in Cic.; cf. molestia): magni sunt oneris; quicquid imponas, vehunt,capable of bearing great burdens,: quae (senectus) plerisque senibus sic odiosa est, ut onus se Aetnā gravius dicant sustinere,: onus atque munus magnum,: hoc onus si vos adlevabitis,: officii,: probandi,the burden of proof, obligation to prove,; : oneri esse,to be a burden,; 15, 33: neque eram nescius, quantis oneribus premerere susceptarum rerum,: epici carminis onera lyrā sustinere,.—
(Eccl. Lat.) The burden of a prophecy, the woes predicted against any one: Babylonis,: Tyri,.—With subj.gen.: Domini,: verbi Domini,.

la:adj:onerarius.html:
ŏnĕrārĭus, a, um, adj.
onus
,
of or belonging to burden, transport, or carriage; that bears a burden, carries freight (class.): jumenta,beasts of burden,: navis, a ship of burden, Sisenn. ap. (opp. actuaria); ; ; .—Also subst.: ŏnĕrārĭa, ae, f., a ship of burden, a merchant-vessel, a transport, .

la:verb:onero.gloss: to burden, lade, load, heap up anything in anything
senses: to burden, lade, load, heap up anything in anything
la:verb:onero.html:
ŏnĕro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
onus
.
To load, lade, burden, freight with any thing (class.).
Lit.: navim magnam multis mercibus,: naves, ad celeritatem onerandi subductionesque, paulo facit humiliores,for loading expeditiously,: jumenta,: naves commeatu, etc.,: costas aselli pomis,: tauri cervix oneratur aratro,is loaded, burdened,: aures lapillis,; cf.: umerum pallio,: ventrem,to load, fill,: epulis onerari,to overload, gorge one's self,: vino et epulis onerati,: cibus, qui in aegritudine alat neque oneret,without oppressing the stomach,: vaccas,to cause them to be covered,.—
Transf., in gen., to load, cover (poet.): dapibus mensas onerare,to cover,: manusque ambas jaculis oneravit acutis,: jaculo palmas oneravit acuto,i. e. armed, (but armavit is the better read.; v. Forbig. ad loc.): membra

sepulcro, ; cf.: ossa aggere terrae,: aliquem saxis,to stone,.—

Trop., to load, burden, weary; to oppress, overwhelm, overload (with good or evil; cf. Forbig. ad ), etc.: me amoenitate oneravit dies,has overwhelmed me,.: laetitiā senem,: malignitateomnis mortalis,: diem commoditatibus,: aliquem mendaciis,; cf. : judicem argumentis,: aethera votis,: verbis lassas onerantibus aures,: aliquem pugnis,: maledictis,; cf. contumeliis,; for which only absol. Sejanum, . 68: aliquem injuriis,: aliquem malis,: aliquem laudibus,: spe praemiorum,: promissis,: honoribus,.—
Transf., to make heavier or more burdensome, to render more oppressive, to heighten, to aggravate (only since the Aug. per.; esp. freq. in Tac. and the younger Plin.): injuriam alicujus invidiā,: pericula alicujus,: curas,: delectum avaritiā et luxu,to aggravate, make worse, render more odious,: onerat te quaesturae tuae famā, quam ex Bithyniā optimam revexisti,; ; ; .—
To load, stow, or heap up any thing in any thing (poet.): vina cadis,: canistris Dona Cereris,.— Hence, ŏnĕrātus, a, um, P. a., filled, full; with gen.: oneratus frugum et floris Liberi, Pac. ap. (Trag. Rel. p. 95 Rib.).—
Loaded, i. e. deceived, befooled: ille est oneratus recte,: ego illum probe jam oneratum huc admovebo,.

la:adj:onustus.gloss: loaded with, laden, burdened, full of (coupled with genitive or ablative)
senses: loaded with, laden, burdened, full of (coupled with genitive or ablative)
la:adj:onustus.html:
ŏnustus (hŏnust-), a, um, adj.
onus
,
loaded, laden, burdened, freighted, etc. (class.).
Lit.: asellus onustus auro, (dub.): naves onustae frumento,: currus quinque liberis,: magna vis camelorum onusta frumenti,.—
Transf.
Filled, full, abounding in: ager praedā onustus,: pharetrae telis,.—
With gen.: auri,.—
Full, satisfied with food (anteclass.): quia sum onusta mei ex sententiā,; : corpus,overloaded,.—
Trop., loaded, burdened (ante-class.): omnes exegit foras onustos fustibus,: corpus,burdened, weighed down with years,: onustum pectus porto laetitiā lubentiāque,: fidicina dolis astutiisque,full of,: corpus hesternis vitiis,.— Sup.: carri onustissimi,.

la:adj:onerosus.html:
ŏnĕrōsus, a, um, adj.
onus
,
burdensome, heavy, oppressive (poet. and in postAug. prose; syn.: gravis, difficilis).
Lit.: praeda,.—Of food that is difficult of digestion and causes oppression: cibus etiam valentibus onerosus,: (ervum) capiti et stomacho onerosum,.— Comp.: aër est onerosior igni,. —
Trop., burdensome, onerous, irksome: onerosior altera sors est,: donatio,: quam sit onerosum succedere bono principi,: consolatores,.—Hence, adv.: ŏnĕrōsē, odiously (post-class.), .—Comp.: onerosius,.
